title: Diodes, transistors and gain
blurb: Explain how diodes pass current one way, how transistors switch and amplify, and what gain means.

T6B01.why: Every conducting diode drops some voltage, and the amount depends on the type: typically about 0.3 V for Schottky, 0.7 V for silicon.
T6B01.trap: A forward drop is normal. It does not mean the diode is broken.

T6B02.why: A **diode** is a one-way valve: current flows anode to cathode but not back.
T6B02.trap: A resistor and a fuse pass current both ways.

T6B03.why: A **transistor** can turn a large current fully on or off with a small control signal, so it works as a switch.
T6B03.trap: A potentiometer is adjusted by hand, not by a signal.

T6B04.why: A bipolar **transistor** is a three-region sandwich (NPN or PNP). Tubes like triodes are not semiconductors.
T6B04.trap: Triode and pentode are vacuum tubes.

T6B05.why: Gate, drain and source are the leads of a **field-effect** transistor.
T6B05.trap: A bipolar junction transistor has base, collector and emitter.

T6B06.why: A printed **stripe** at one end of the diode body marks the cathode.
T6B06.trap: Look for a stripe, not for the word or a letter.

T6B07.why: An LED glows when **forward current** passes through it. Reverse current blocks.
T6B07.trap: Coupled RF does not light an LED. Forward current does.

T6B08.why: FET stands for **Field Effect Transistor**: a voltage on the gate creates a field that controls current.

T6B09.why: A diode's two electrodes are the **anode** and the **cathode**.
T6B09.trap: Source, drain, gate and base are transistor leads. A diode has just two electrodes.

T6B10.why: A **transistor** is an active part: a small input controls a larger output, so it gives power gain.
T6B10.trap: Passive parts (transformer, resistor, reactor) can't make more power than they receive.

T6B11.why: Gain is output compared with input, and that can be voltage, current or power. **All three** are correct.

T6B12.why: A bipolar transistor's electrodes are the **emitter, base and collector**.
T6B12.trap: Gate, drain and source are FET names.
